question: The ischaemic penumbra is the zone of irreversibly infarcted brain tissue at the core of an ischaemic stroke that cannot benefit from reperfusion.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. The penumbra is the metabolically compromised but potentially salvageable tissue around the infarct core. It is the biological basis of the therapeutic window for thrombolysis and thrombectomy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually, that statement is false. The ischaemic penumbra is the SALVAGEABLE zone of hypoperfused but electrically silent tissue surrounding the irreversibly infarcted core. It is the penumbra, not the core, that reperfusion therapy aims to rescue.
